anomalies: THE FIRST SWEEP OF TODAY MISSED AUSTRALIA, AND IT WAS THERE. runs/2026-08-16.json records 'Australia (nothing in window)' and says Australian coverage was searched via Grain Central and GIWA. The GIWA August crop report was published on Grain Central on 2026-08-14, inside the window, and yielded six rows including the state harvest cut from 22.66 Mt to 21.01 Mt. Not a criticism of that run, which was thorough elsewhere — it is the concrete case for what a same-day re-run is for, and it is worth a human noting that a source can be named as searched and still be missed.

GIWA WAS NOT IN source_manifest.json AT ALL. The manifest carries ABARES for Australia, which is quarterly and silent since June. GIWA publishes monthly through the season and is the source that actually moved this week. Added to the manifest with rhythm 'monthly', last_publication 2026-08-14. A human should confirm that is the right rhythm.

SECOND SCHEMA GAP OF THE DAY: NO CROP VALUE FOR HOPS OR SUNFLOWER. Two real, in-window, weather-attributed facts were found and deliberately NOT recorded because the controlled crop vocabulary has nowhere correct to put them. Plzensky Prazdroj, the largest Czech brewer, expects losses this year from a stunted hop yield, with its sustainability manager saying three bad years in a row would be an existential problem for hop growers. And Romanian sunflowers, being heat- and drought-tolerant, yielded plentifully — a favourable row. Filing either under mixed_grains or field_veg would have been wrong. Reported rather than mis-typed. This follows the condition_very_poor_poor gap a human closed earlier today.

A THIRD SCHEMA GAP: NO METRIC FOR A MACRO-ECONOMIC LOSS. The Triodos estimate of a 1% EU GDP hit, about 180 billion euros, is the largest single number in the corpus this week and metric_name has no value for it. Filed under 'cost' with direction 'up' and a caveated flag explaining the mapping (t007). A gdp_impact metric would fix it.

A LEVEL-VERSUS-DELTA PROBLEM IN planted_area. t013 records Idaho potato planted_area as 15,000, but that is 15,000 acres FEWER than last year, not an area. It is the only form the source gives. Flagged caveated with the unit string carrying the warning, and it sits in its own single-reading FreshPlaza series so it cannot silently join a level series — but the schema does not distinguish the two and a human should decide whether it should.

THREE FIGURES DELIBERATELY LEFT UNQUANTIFIED, following the s036 precedent: 'less than 150mm year to date' (WA rainfall, a bound), 'down by about one-third' (Zeeland potato harvest, a fraction that would have to be converted), and '1.5 to 2 tons per hectare' (Bosnian maize, a range whose midpoint would be invented). All three keep their numbers in the quote and the summary. t004, t008, t009.

TWO PRICE ROWS WHOSE WEIGHT BASIS THE SOURCE DOES NOT STATE. t015 (Dutch red onions, 45 cents) and t016 (Dutch potatoes, 35 cents) are both quoted as bare cents. Per kilo is the trade convention but the article does not say so, so the unit string carries the caveat rather than assuming. t016's attribution is 'implied' rather than 'weather_explicit' because that particular sentence does not itself name the weather, though the article's headline and framing do.

ZERO MERGES ON A RE-RUN. All 16 claim_keys were free. On a same-day re-run STEP 1B says to expect most finds to merge as corroboration rather than insert. The opposite happened, which is itself the finding: the two sweeps of today did not overlap at all, because they searched differently rather than searching again.

ARGENTINA AND INDIA PRODUCED ZERO ROWS ACROSS BOTH RUNS TODAY. Argentina is in the manifest as a weekly-in-season source (Buenos Aires Grain Exchange) and nothing published in this window was reachable from either run. India's seasonal sources last published 31 July and 4 August, just before window_start. Neither is obviously a failed search, but two named STEP 3 regions being empty twice in one day is worth a human eye.
REUTERS AND BLOOMBERG REMAIN UNREACHABLE, as reported by the first run of today and on 2026-08-10. Standing limitation.
NO ROW HAS AN EVENT_DATE MORE THAN A YEAR BEFORE ITS PUBLISHED_DATE. The largest gap among these 16 is one day.

NO KEY COLLISIONS AND NO SUFFIXING. The nine unquantified rows took nine distinct fortnight keys, separated by country and by hazard_type: the two Western Australian unquantified rows differ by hazard (frost vs drought) and the two favourable ones by crop (mixed_grains vs oats), so no two collapsed onto one key.

THIRTEEN SERIES NOW HAVE MORE THAN ONE READING AND NO LABEL, up from twelve. The new one is the Western Australian GIWA production series, listed below with the other twelve carried over from the first run. Each is chartable:false and stays off Tab 2 until a human writes a label. chartable count is unchanged at 5.

VALIDATOR NOT RUN. STEP 8B forbids running any script in the repo, which includes validate.py, so it was not executed. The checks it would perform were reimplemented independently for this run's rows: flag_status/flag_note paired both ways, review_flag dual-written identically, every quantified row carrying an event_date, series_key and verbatim quote, every badge resolved against badge_map.json by the documented match rule, no duplicate ids, and every shard compared field-for-field against all.json. notes_on_judgement_calls: The AP European drought wire was read on wsls.com. apnews.com, france24.com, thehill.com, nationalobserver.com and abcnews all either failed to return a body or are equally unmapped; no host in badge_map.json carries this wire. wsls.com is not in the drop list, so per STEP 7 the row keeps source_badge 'Press', origin_publisher is set to Associated Press, and the host is appended to unmapped_domains.json as a worklist item. No 'unverified' flag was set on those rows: an unmapped domain is a worklist item, not a fault in the number.

GIWA rows cite the Grain Central article (Trade, mapped) as the document read, because that is where the prose sentences containing the figures are, with publisher and origin_publisher set to GIWA so the series stays on the agency and does not fork. This follows the precedent the first run set for the USDA rows via DTN.

The two single-farm rows that carry numbers in their quotes (Zeeland potatoes, Bosnian maize) were left unquantified rather than given farm-level series. Even had the figures been point values, a single farm does not belong in a national yield series — but the deciding reason is that neither figure is a point value.

Elveden Estate's 20% reservoir reading IS quantified and does get a series, keyed on the estate as its region, so it cannot collide with the Environment Agency's national England reservoir series. This is exactly the case the 'region MUST be included' rule in STEP 5 exists for.
month was set from published_date for all 16 rows, matching the dominant corpus convention and the first run of today.
